skill: Squares and cubes of small integers
description: Instantly recalling n² for n from 1 to 20 and n³ for n from 1 to 10, such as 17² = 289 and 9³ = 729.
Instantly recalling the values of 2ⁿ for n from 1 to 10, up to 2¹⁰ = 1024.
Instantly recalling n! for n from 1 to 7, up to 7! = 5040.

Converting between common fractions (halves, thirds, quarters, fifths, sixths, sevenths, eighths, ninths, tenths, twelfths, twentieths) and their terminating or repeating decimals, such as 1/7 = 0.142857 repeating.

skill: Decimal equivalents of common square roots (2,3, 5, and 10)

description: Writing integers as products of prime powers and deciding that a divides b exactly when each prime's exponent in a is at most its exponent in b.

skill: Primality testing up to the square root
description: Deciding whether a positive integer a is prime by checking divisibility only by primes p with p² ≤ a.

skill: Counting divisors from the prime factorization
description: Finding how many positive divisors n has by adding one to each exponent in its prime factorization and multiplying the results.

skill: Sum of divisors from the prime factorization
description: Finding the sum of all positive divisors of n by multiplying, for each prime, the sum of its powers from p⁰ up to p^e, optionally using the geometric series formula (p^(e+1) − 1)/(p − 1).
Using digit-based rules to decide divisibility by 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11, such as digit sums for 3 and 9, the last two or three digits for 4 and 8, and the alternating digit sum for 11.
Finding gcd(a, b) or lcm(a,b) using prime factorization; recognizing gcd(a,b)*lcm(a,b) = a*b
For relatively prime a and b, identifying ab − a − b as the largest integer that cannot be written as as + bt with nonnegative integers s and t.

skill: Remainders and the meaning of mod
description: Interpreting x mod n as the remainder when x is divided by n.
Finding remainders of sums and products by first reducing each term or factor mod n and then combining the reduced values.
Adapting the digit-based divisibility tests for divisors from 2 through 13. (note that 7 and 13 do not use individual digits but split the number into two pieces)
Finding the nth term of a sequence that repeats a block of k terms by reducing the position (n − 1) mod k.

skill: nth term of an arithmetic sequence
description: Using a + (n − 1)d to find a term, the common difference, or a term's position in a sequence with constant difference d.

skill: nth term of a geometric sequence
description: Using arⁿ⁻¹ to find a term or the common ratio of a sequence with constant ratio r.
Summing 1 + 2 + … + n with n(n + 1)/2.
Counting the terms as (last − first)/d + 1 and multiplying that count by the average of the first and last terms.
Summing 1 + r + r² + … + rⁿ with (rⁿ⁺¹ − 1)/(r − 1).
Evaluating n² − (n − 1)² + (n − 2)² − … ± 1² as n(n + 1)/2 by pairing consecutive squares.

skill: Egyptian fractions by the greedy algorithm
description: Writing a positive fraction as a sum of distinct unit fractions by repeatedly subtracting the largest unit fraction 1/(q + 1) that fits, where q is the quotient when b is divided by a.

skill: Splitting unit fractions and telescoping sums

description: Counting the ordered arrangements of n distinct things as n!.

skill: Permutations of k objects from n
description: Counting ordered selections of k distinct things from n distinct things with nPk = n!/(n − k)!.
Counting ordered sequences of k choices from n distinct options when repeats are allowed, which is n multiplied by itself k times.
Counting unordered selections of k distinct things from n distinct things with n!/(k!(n − k)!).
Counting unordered selections of k items from n types when duplicates are allowed with C(n + k − 1, k).
Building Pascal's triangle by adding adjacent entries and reading binomial coefficients from its rows.
Using the facts that each row of Pascal's triangle sums to a power of 2 and that the first five rows give the digits of the powers of 11.
Counting the paths through a directed grid or graph by working backward from the finish and labeling each node with the number of paths from it to the finish.
Factoring or expanding with x² − y² = (x − y)(x + y).

skill: Sum and difference of cubes factoring
description: Factoring with x³ − y³ = (x − y)(x² + xy + y²) and x³ + y³ = (x + y)(x² − xy + y²).

skill: Fast mental arithmetic with difference of squares
description: Speeding up products and squares near round numbers, such as 97 · 103 = 100² − 3² and 97² = (97 + 3)(97 − 3) + 3².
Expanding (x + y)ⁿ using binomial coefficients from the corresponding row of Pascal's triangle.

skill: Maximum or minimum of a quadratic
description: Finding where ax² + bx + c reaches its maximum or minimum, at x = −b/(2a), and evaluating the extreme value.

skill: Maximizing a product with a fixed sum
description: Using the principle that two positive numbers with a constant sum have a larger product the closer together they are.

skill: Sum and product of quadratic roots
description: Finding the sum (−b/a) and product (c/a) of the roots of ax² + bx + c = 0 without solving the equation.

skill: Probability as favorable over total outcomes
description: Computing the probability of an event by dividing the number of favorable outcomes by the size of the sample space of equally likely outcomes.
Using the side ratios 1 : 1 : √2 and 1 : √3 : 2, and their multiples, to find missing sides.
Spotting the triples 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 7-24-25, 8-15-17, 9-40-41, and 20-21-29, and their multiples, to find right-triangle sides without computation.
Using the fact that the diagonal of a unit cube is √3, so a cube with side s has a space diagonal of s√3.

skill: Angle pairs formed by a transversal
description: Identifying vertical, adjacent, corresponding, alternate interior, alternate exterior, same-side interior, and same-side exterior angles where a transversal crosses two lines.
Using the fact that two lines cut by a transversal are parallel exactly when the corresponding angle groups (1, 4, 5, 8 and 2, 3, 6, 7) are congruent, to find unknown angles or prove lines parallel.

skill: Area and volume ratios of similar figures
description: Finding area ratios as the square, and volume ratios as the cube, of the side-length ratio of similar figures.

skill: Circumference and area of a circle
description: Applying C = πd = 2πr and A = πr².

skill: Area of squares, rectangles, and parallelograms
description: Applying A = s² for squares and A = bh for rectangles and parallelograms.
Applying A = (b₁ + b₂)h/2 using the two parallel bases and the height.

skill: Area of a triangle from base and height
description: Applying A = ½bh for any triangle.
Applying A = (√3/4)s² from the side length alone.
Finding a triangle's area from its three side lengths with √(s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)), where s is the semiperimeter.

skill: Triangle area from inradius and semiperimeter
description: Applying A = rs to relate a triangle's area, its inscribed circle's radius, and its semiperimeter.

skill: Surface area and volume of a sphere
description: Applying SA = 4πr² and V = (4/3)πr³.
Applying V = (base area)·h for rectangular prisms and V = πr²h for cylinders.
Applying V = ⅓πr²h for cones and V = ⅓(base area)·h for pyramids.
Using a² + b² = c² to find a missing hypotenuse, c = √(a² + b²), or a missing leg, a = √(c² − b²).

skill: Right triangles inscribed in a circle
description: Using the fact that a triangle with a diameter as one side and its third vertex on the circle is a right triangle, and that the midpoint of a right triangle's hypotenuse is equidistant from all three vertices.

skill: Platonic solids: faces, edges, and vertices
description: Recalling the numbers of faces, edges, and vertices of the tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, and icosahedron.
Always submitting a guess on unknown problems because there is no penalty, especially when only a few answers are possible.
Use the structure of the question to establish how large or small the answer could be
Passing over problems that look long, answering easier ones first, and returning to the skipped ones if time remains.
Replacing an obvious but lengthy computation with a quicker route, such as factoring out a common term with the distributive law: 43(17) + 57(17) = 100(17).
Keeping numbers small by factoring and canceling common factors in a fraction before multiplying out the numerator and denominator.

skill: Knowing when not to hunt for shortcuts
description: Doing the direct computation instead of searching for a clever method when the obvious solution takes under 30 seconds.

skill: Using the required answer form as a hint
description: Inferring the answer's likely type from the requested form (integer if no form is given, non-integer if a mixed number is requested, radicals or π if those forms are requested) and using it to catch errors such as wrong units.
Approaching competitions with enjoyment and a relaxed attitude, following the sheet's closing advice to have fun.
